listing.description_html:
Before you raise prices, see how many sales you could lose and still earn more, and what profit each increase gives at the loss you actually expect.

Because a price increase goes straight to margin, the answer is often larger than people expect. This workbook calculates it for up to eight increases: the most sales you could lose and still make the same gross profit, and the monthly profit at the loss you actually expect.

What's included

  • Up to eight price-increase scenarios side by side
  • Maximum share of sales you can lose and still keep today's gross profit
  • Monthly profit at the sales loss you actually expect, and the change against today
  • Uses your real variable and fixed costs
  • Works for products, services and subscriptions
  • PDF guide with a worked example and a field-by-field reference

Who it's for

  • Service businesses and agencies reviewing their rates
  • Online sellers and shops with rising supplier costs
  • Subscription businesses considering a new price for new or existing customers
  • Anyone who has not raised prices in a year or more

You get: price_increase_impact_calculator.xlsx (Current, Scenarios) and this guide.

Works in Excel 2016 or later, Excel for Mac and Excel on the web; opens in Google Sheets and LibreOffice.

This workbook is a planning tool, not financial advice. It models profit from the costs and volumes you enter; real customer response to a price change is uncertain, so test increases carefully.
